name: Confraternity / burial and sickness fund
key_source: PARKED, NOT CODED. Gazzini 2020 (10.17464/9788867742967_04), read in full: aid is usually a 'ragionevole aspettativa' rather than an enforceable right, funded by entry fees, annual dues, fines, legacies and invested property, covering illness, infirmity, old age, burial, unemployment, debt, work damage, theft of livestock, robbery on trade routes, ransom from pirates and bandits, legal costs and imprisonment. Verification is EX ANTE where it exists: the Milanese Camera dei mercanti checked which road a robbed merchant had taken and excluded him if it was not an approved one. Contrast guild_box_brabant, where relief is an entitlement verified ex post by home visit. Code once the entitlement gradient can be set against van Leeuwen 2012. REGIONAL LIMIT, ADDED 2026-08-13 FROM KLIEBER 2001 (Salzburg, 1600-1950, read but not coded; see logbook 2): the Italian pattern does not generalise. Post-Tridentine Salzburg confraternities were death-service bodies whose material relief was 'ein eher bescheidenes und eindeutig nachrangiges Engagement' - one Liebesbund reserved up to ten per cent of expenditure for alms, and only from the 1770s. Klieber ties this to the medieval linkage of alms to totendienstliche Agenden and states that the charitable dimension survived more strongly in the Romance lands. CONSEQUENCE FOR CODING: this cannot be one row for Latin Christendom. When coded it must be split regionally, on the tontine_en/tontine_fr precedent.

name: English religious gild relief
key_source: McRee 1993 (Journal of British Studies 32:3, 195-225, 10.1086/386030), read in full, working from the returns to the royal inquiry into English gilds of 1388-89 (PRO C.47). Relief is need-assessed and desert-assessed rather than an entitlement on a defined event, which is what separates this form from both guild boxes. name: Friendly society / box club
key_source: Prom 2010 (The Historian 72:4, 888-908, 10.1111/J.1540-6563.2010.00280.X), read in full from lodge minute and fines books of the Oddfellows and the Free Gardeners in Durham, Northumberland and Yorkshire. THE FORM THAT SETTLES THE VF1 QUESTION: the sick visitor is a FELLOW MEMBER and he verifies both condition and conduct, so mode and object come apart within a single form. Later than the census's centre of gravity — Prom's window is c.1870-1914 — and coded from a study of discipline, so contribution rates and actuarial structure are absent. SUPERSEDED INSTRUCTION: this row previously said Rusnock & Dietz 2012 would fill CN2 and PR1. It does not, and must not — Rusnock's societies are women's clubs of 1780-1830 and are coded separately as friendly_society_female_england. The two forms differ on CN3, PY3 and PR1, and filling one from the other would have produced that agreement by construction. Broten 2012 is still in the collection and is still the right source for PR1, being on the financial viability of these same lodges.

name: Gildebus — guild sickness, burial, old-age and widows fund
key_source: van Leeuwen 2012 (Economic History Review 65:1, 61-90, 10.1111/j.1468-0289.2011.00602.x), read in full. 225 sickness schemes extant in 1811, 150 of them guild-run; average fund age 112 years. THE SOURCE THAT FILLS HZ1, LS1 AND THE MORAL-HAZARD MATERIAL. NOT INDEPENDENT OF guild_box_brabant: Masure records that these funds appeared centuries earlier in the Southern Netherlands and flourished in the North only from the late sixteenth century, so descent from the Brabantine boxes is plausible and the two must not be counted as independent evidence.

name: Craft pensions and supply, incorporation of Mary's Chapel
key_source: Allen 2022 (Scottish Historical Review 101:2, 10.3366/shr.2022.0561), read in full from the incorporation's minutes and discharged accounts, ECA SL34. Discretionary relief on petition — quarterly pensions and one-off 'supply' — granted 'during their pleasure'. FIRST HALF OF A PAIR: Allen's argument is that the 1768 widows' fund existed to convert this into an entitlement. NOT the Scottish Ministers' Widows' Fund of 1744; that is widows_fund_scotland, which Allen only cites.

name: Widows' fund annuity scheme, incorporation of Mary's Chapel
key_source: Allen 2022, 237-239. Adopted 8 March 1768 by forty-three votes to thirteen, designed with Dr Alexander Webster, an architect of the 1744 ministers' fund. Target capital £5,500 sterling from quarterly subscriptions plus the incorporation's own funds and the deacons'; first annuities only to widows of contributors dying after Martinmas 1774; thereafter 'an equally divided portion of its annual produce'. SECOND HALF OF A PAIR — opposite values to craft_pension_edinburgh on MB3, PY1, PY3 and LS2.

name: Female friendly society
key_source: Rusnock & Dietz 2012 (Journal of Women's History 24:1, 60-85), read in full, working from thirty-nine sets of printed rules for female friendly societies, 1780-1830. CODED AS A SEPARATE FORM RATHER THAN USED TO FILL friendly_society_england's THIN CELLS, AND THE REASON MATTERS: Prom's lodges are mixed-sex or male and his window is 1870-1914, while these are women's clubs a century earlier. Filling one form's .NR from another form's source would have manufactured agreement between two populations that were never observed together. The two now separate on CN3 (P against 1), PY3 (1 against P) and PR1 (0 against P), which is the discriminant evidence that filling would have destroyed. Carries the census's first TAPERED benefit schedule and its clearest ex-ante peril pricing in a membership fund.

name: Avarız akçesi vakfı (neighbourhood fund)
key_source: Küçük 2025 (Osmanlı Medeniyeti Araştırmaları Dergisi 24, 147-183, 10.21021/osmed.1472954), read in full, from the Kırkçeşme mahallesi avarız akçesi vakıf defteri in the Milli Kütüphane manuscript collection plus the kaza's other avarız records, population registers and şer'iyye sicilleri; disbursements dated 1841. Turkish-language source. THE BLANKET CONFIDENCE CAP IMPOSED ON THIS BATCH ON 2026-08-13 IS WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY, AND THE REASONING BEHIND IT WAS WRONG. Capping confidence because the reviewer could not read the language conflated two things: confidence records the strength of the EVIDENCE, and reviewability is a fact about the PROJECT, now carried by review_status and reviewed_by. A cell resting on an unambiguous figure is not less well evidenced because nobody has yet checked it. The confidences here were in practice set on evidential grounds and are left as they stand - the low on RB3 is a source-critical judgement about scribal formulae, not a language penalty, and GV1 is .NR because Küçük is silent, not because he is Turkish. MS reports (2026-08-13) that the Synergy team will include a PI reading Turkish and Arabic, so these rows are reviewable in principle and should be an early target for review_status=source-checked. THE FORM THAT BREAKS THE CONTRIBUTION ASSUMPTION: capitalised once at 6,280 kuruş and living on a 942 kuruş annual nema, with expenditure from principal categorically forbidden, so CN1 is .NA and MC1 is allocation rather than pooling. Perils covered run from earthquake, flood and fire to paupers' funerals, orphans' marriage portions and the tax share of the household that cannot pay. SPLIT CANDIDATE, NOT YET EVIDENCED: Küçük states that avarız funds were capitalised EITHER by wealthy donors OR as an aid fund the inhabitants formed among themselves; the second variant would take MC1=pooling and needs its own row when a case is found.

name: Cash waqf / para vakfı (parent instrument)
key_source: PARKED, NOT CODED IN THIS CENSUS, AND THE REASON IS A BOUNDARY DECISION. Deniz 2026 (10.33227/auifd.1740727), read in full on 97 sixteenth-century vakfiyes from 35 registers across Istanbul, Üsküdar, Bursa, Trabzon, Antep, Halep, Konya, Balat and Avlonya: 77 of the 97 are fully charitable, 3 are pure family endowments, the rest hybrid, and the beneficiaries named are imams, students and the poor. THE CASH WAQF IS A FUNDING VEHICLE WHOSE PURPOSE VARIES, NOT A HAZARD POOL - the same instrument endows a mosque, a lineage, or a quarter's collective obligations, and only the last is loss mitigation. Its place is organizational_forms beside waqf_khayri and waqf_ahli: endowed perpetual capital, an inalienable corpus, a mütevelli under a nazır, hereditary trusteeship, and a contested legal validity settled by Ebussuud on örf grounds against Çivizade's prohibition. OPERATING MECHANICS RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THEY BEAR ON RB3: profit rates 10 per cent in 77 per cent of deeds, none above 15 or below 10, the legal ceiling confirmed in Ebussuud's Ma'rūżāt; security either kafīl (in most deeds kafīl-i malī, a guarantor with property, materially liable rather than merely producing the debtor) or rahn (rahn-i qawī, a pledge sufficiently valuable and free of competing claims). Coded as a loss-mitigation form only through avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme, which is one. ÇİZAKÇA 1995 (JESHO 38:3, 313-354, 10.1163/1568520952600407) read in full via OCR, and it is the English-language anchor for this material. Bursa court registers 1555-1823, TRANSACTIONS RATHER THAN DEEDS, which is why it can do what the vakfiye studies cannot. Three results. (1) PERPETUITY: of 761 individually identified cash waqfs, 148 survived more than a century, a 19 per cent perpetuity rate that Çizakça calls a probable minimum; he notes the comparison Ebussuud invited, against real-estate waqfs, has never been attempted. (2) SECURITY IN PRACTICE WAS REAL ESTATE: istiğlal, the ordinary Bursa device, is a loan against a piece of real estate conveyed as a notional sale and leased back at a 'rent' of often exactly ten per cent - so the rahn/kefil formula in the deeds does not describe what actually secured the advance. (3) Bursa's own avarız-ı mahalle funds are in his dataset with capital figures across 1078-1239 AH, a longitudinal series and the obvious test of endowment erosion. Whether these waqfs lent at interest is disputed between Barkan-Ayverdi, Mandaville and Gerber against jurists who hold the historians misread the terminology; held open, not coded.

name: Bodemerij (Amsterdam notarial practice: contract van bodemerij and bodemerijbrief)
key_source: Winkelman (ed.) 1983, Bronnen tot de geschiedenis van den Oostzeehandel, RGP Grote Serie 184/185/186: nrs 946-962, 1991-2005, 3227-3242 (46 of 48 acts read - 36 contracten van bodemerij, 10 protesten; no. 946 wanting and no. 947 fragmentary in the copy consulted); Winkelman's Inleiding, quoting A. Verwer and J. Wagenaar. Boundary reading: Frankot 2007 and 2010 (methodological only - neither discusses bodemerij).
